title: Gamifying CodeC: Examining Competitive and Cooperative Learning in Computer Programming
abstract: Gamification has emerged as one of the most notable advancements on employing game elements in non-gaming contexts to target and improve behavioral engagements. However, most gamified applications are focused on competitive game features and, thus, applying game mechanics with little regard to the psychological aspects that connect the mechanics to target outcomes. This is where cooperative gamification has yet to be explored, especially in learning platforms, to integrate motivators into the instruction of programming. The study is a quantitative experiment on competitive and cooperative gamification using an online teaching and learning platform named CodeC. It analyzes the role of competitive and cooperative gamification on task effort, enjoyment, and social relatedness using the Social Interdependence Theory. In the course of 7 days, 54 participants were assigned to competitive and cooperative code rooms in CodeC. Data was gathered from first-year programming students of the Ateneo de Naga University - College of Computer Studies through questionnaires and the platform. The findings revealed a significant difference between the two setups in task effort, with higher scores in the competitive setup. Meanwhile, no significant differences were found in task interest and social relatedness. This entails that competitive and cooperative gamification can effectively motivate interest in learning programming and social relatedness among learners in the same group. The results indicate the importance of gamification in education in general for improving task interest, specifically task effort in a competitive setup.

title: FLOU: Evaluating the Intrinsic Motivation of Learners in Gamifying Academic Programs through a Gamified Mobile Application
abstract: Learning is influenced by various motivational factors and the contemporary trend of employing gamification in education to enhance student engagement and motivation. While gamification integrates game elements into non-game contexts to create immersive learning experiences, it faces challenges in sustaining students’ motivation in the long run. Often, students initially respond positively to gamified platforms but later exhibit low intrinsic motivation, emphasizing the need to address this issue. This research delves into the relationship between intrinsic motivation and gamified academic experiences, drawing upon motivational theories and psychological principles - most importantly from the Self-Determination Theory (SDT) on Intrinsic Motivation. It seeks to strike a balance between intrinsic and extrinsic motivators in the design of gamified educational platforms to foster enduring and profound learning experiences. The objective of this research is to evaluate the intrinsic motivation of students within a gamified academic platform, called Flou, and apply motivational theories and gamification frameworks to create a balanced gamified experience. The study offers insights into designing gamified platforms that enhance students’ intrinsic motivation and engagement while promoting meaningful educational outcomes. The study concludes that the gamified platform did not exhibit an effect to the motivation of users. It did not necessarily lead to higher levels of intrinsic motivation or engagement compared to those who did not use the application. Moreover, the implored user-centric gamified design on Intrinsic Motivators had little to no interactions among the user–with which only elements from Competence have found to have most engagements from the user (mainly attaining badges). The findings of the study are used to formulate recommendations towards the design of a balanced gamification to be used in an educational context. This study aims to contribute to the evolving field of gamification in education by addressing the challenge of sustaining students’ motivation and promoting self-directed learning within gamified platforms.

title: EdGagement: Gamifying Teacher Engagement in the Workplace
abstract: Gamification in the workplace is a concept that incorporates game elements into tasks performed by employees to make work more interesting and fun. It aims to make work more likable and less stressful. The proposed project aims to gamify the workplace in the context of teachers. Studies have shown that the duties of a teacher do not revolve around the four corners of the classroom. It involves considerably more than classroom instruction, such as committee work, attendance at meetings and training, and crafting policies. Just like any other employee, teachers may experience burnout in the long run and be less productive. EdGagement is a web application that taps the three primary motivators (accomplishments, sense of collaboration, and recognition) to improve teachers’ engagement. It provides a platform for sharing achievements, managing work progress, and building cooperation. Currently, the application offers five different modules: system administration management of tasks, users, and badges, dean monitoring of faculty progress and performance, chairpersons management and monitoring of departmental activities and faculty performance, teacher management of their progress and improvement, and beadle/co-beadle management of teacher classroom tasks. Based from the result of the usability study, the Dean system received an average SUS score of 92.5, beadle/co-beadle system received an average SUS score of 80.5, teacher system received an average SUS score of 80, and lastly, the chairperson system received an average SUS score of 72.5. In conclusion, the EdGagement system received an 81 out of 100 rating, indicating an excellent usability system based on the System Usability Scale standards. This project is beneficial to any university that is willing to adapt gamification to encourage more motivation and performance from their faculty. It highlights the importance of making work fun and enjoyable even in workplaces.

title: PROJECT PASIL: A Machine Learning-Driven Game for Grade 4 - 6 Students Through Project Personalized Adaptive System for Integer Learning
abstract: Mathematics continues to pose challenges for many students. Conventional teaching approaches often follow a uniform instructional sequence, which may not accommodate diverse learning speeds. This “one-size-fits-all” approach can lead to student disengagement, as learners may become frustrated when tasks are too difficult or bored when they are too easy. To address these challenges, this study developed an educational game focused on the Order of Operations that dynamically adjusts difficulty to improve learning outcomes and sustain engagement. The research compared a traditional game-based learning (GBL) intervention with fixed difficulty levels against an AI-based version powered by Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). PPO was selected for its computational efficiency and stability, enabling real-time adaptation to a student’s level of expertise. The study was conducted with students from a private basic education institution in Naga City. The results from an independent samples t-test showed that the experimental group achieved a higher mean gain score (M = 9.40) compared to the control group (M = 6.50). Although the difference did not reach statistical significance (t(18) = −1.619, p = .123), the moderate-to-large effect size (d = 0.724) suggests a practically meaningful trend in favor of the PPO-based intervention, particularly given the compressed 2-week intervention window and the study’s modest sample size. Furthermore, behavioral analytics revealed high levels of engagement across the intervention, with an average session duration of nearly 22 minutes. Validation of the Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents confirmed their capability of appropriately adjusting game difficulty and generalizing across student profiles. The deployment validation showed that the RL agents maintained lower performance deviation compared to fixed-difficulty systems, while internal validation demonstrated that the agents adapted to both familiar and held-out student profiles with minimal performance degradation. Overall, these findings indicate a promising direction for integrating Reinforcement Learning into adaptive game-based learning environments. The results provide preliminary support for the feasibility of PPO-driven difficulty adjustment as a personalized learning mechanism, and contribute a validated technical framework for future research on RL-based adaptivity in mathematics education.

title: Bridging Communication Gaps: An Adaptive Gamified Platform for Filipino Sign Language Learning
abstract: Even with the formal recognition of Filipino Sign Language (FSL) under Republic Act 11106, around 70% of Filipinos with hearing impairments lack FSL proficiency, and existing learning tools remain limited to static tutorials that neither adapt to individual needs neither to sustain engagement. Senyas was built to address this, web-based platform for FSL alphabet learning integrating real-time gesture recognition, three difficulty adjustment mechanisms, and inclusive gamification features for users like Deaf and hearing learners. A custom Deep Neural Network trained on MediaPipe hand landmark coordinates is used for festure recognition. Three difficulty modes are implemented and compared; static, which delivers a fixed lesson sequence; dynamic, scales task complexity in real time based on recognition accuracy; and AI-driven, builds an additive learner profile focuses on signs the learner struggles the most. Points, badges, progress tracking, and cooperative challenge options is designed to be alternatives to competitive leaderboards are based on Self-Determination Theory, Flow Theory, and Cognitive Load Theory. This is a developmental-experimental design with pilot testing conducted involving exactly 30 college student participants. Quantitative data from system logs and Likert-scale questionnaires were analyzed using ANOVA, paired t-test, and Pearson correlation. Results shows that the feasibility of bringing together the gesture recognition, adaptive learning, and inclusive gamification can work together in a accessible FSL learning platform, achieving a mean gesture recognition accuracy of 84.4% and a statistically significant pre-to-post-test improvement (p = 1.22 × 10^−4) around all participants.

title: Detecting Wheel-Spinning During the Early Stages of Solving Programming Problems
abstract: Wheel-spinning is a phenomenon where a student attempts to solve a problem, takes a considerable amount of time struggling in the process, and becomes stuck for not learning the skill. Novice programmers experience this unproductive persistence as they master problem-solving and programming skills. Prior studies have shown that detecting wheel-spinning can provide meaningful feedback to students as they master a skill. This ongoing research aims to develop a model to detect wheel-spinning in the early stages of code development and testing in solving problems in programming.

title: Sentiment Analysis for Mixed English-Tagalog Online Product Reviews using Lexicon and Machine Learning Approaches
abstract: As E-commerce becomes more popular, the researchers of this study decided to do sentiment analysis for Mixed English-Tagalog Product Reviews to provide visual data to products with user reviews that are composed of Tagalog and English Language. The researchers will try to explore and compare two different methods for doing sentiment analysis such as the Lexicon-based, Machine Learning and Logistic Regression to find out which one gives a satisfactory high and unsatisfactory performance. The study will give an impact to e-commerce store users to have a better understanding when it comes to customers and sellers to improve quality of service and to avoid disappointment upon purchasing a product.

title: Taglish-Aware Fake News Detection: Extension
abstract: This thesis investigates Taglish fake news detection using a controlled 4→4 ablation over multilingual transformer models and training strategies. Four model families (DistilBERT, RoBERTa-Tagalog, mBERT, XLM-R) were each trained under four conditions: Baseline +Paraphrase, +Adversarial, and +Paraphrase+Adversarial. Evaluation used both an in-domain FNF test set (n = 601) and an out-of-domain (OOD) real-world Facebook set (n = 49) comprising posts from established Philippine news outlets, government agencies, and unverified or satirical pages. Results show a substantial generalization gap between in-domain and out-of-domain performance (mean gap = 23.39 percentage points), and weak rank alignment across settings. Adversarial augmentation improved real-world weighted F1 in three model families, while combined paraphrase+adversarial training was not consistently beneficial. DistilBERT +Adv was selected for deployment due to near-top out-of-domain performance with lower inference overhead, and was integrated into a local-inference Chrome extension. Given the small out-of-domain sample, comparative OOD results are interpreted as descriptive rather than definitive pairwise superiority claims.

title: Transformers for Taglish Political Gaslighting: Binary Detection, Tactic Classification, and Zero-Shot Transfer
abstract: The constant combination of Tagalog and English (“Taglish”) in Philippine online discourse confounds the automated detection of harmful language, particularly in political gaslighting where facts and opinions rapidly alter. In this study, we evaluate three transformer models, namely, XLM-R, mBERT, and RoBERTa-Tagalog, on a curated, hand-labeled dataset of approximately 2,800 Taglish Reddit posts across three tasks: (1) binary detection of political gaslighting, (2) multiclass tactic classification, and (3) zero-shot cross-domain transfer to non-political contexts (cultural and historical/revisionist cases). We have conducted a statistical analysis using Cochran’s Q test (p = 0.289 for binary; p = 0.338 for multiclass), and it revealed no significant variance in overall precision among models. We have seen that all three architectures substantiates a highly proficient and statistically comparable baseline for binary detection, with peak performance reaching a Macro-F1 score of 0.82. However, multiclass evaluation exposes an unmistakable ”complexity gap,” where models competently identify overt threats like coercion but fundamentally struggle to process implicit psychological manipulation such as trivialization. Moreover, zero-shot transfer evaluation presented a severe cross-domain vulnerability. Although the models maintained baseline performance in revisionist contexts, they suffered an extreme generalization collapse in the cultural domain due to their incapacity to unravel ”semantic camouflage”; a phenomenon where abusers weaponize positive Filipino traits and cultural norms. These findings suggest that language-specific pretraining is inadequate without domain-specific fine-tuning, offering critical insights to guide future Taglish moderation tools.

title: Assessing the Effects of AI-Generated Reviews on Product Ratings Through RoBERTa Detection
abstract: This study investigated the detection of AI-generated product reviews on e-commerce platforms using a fine-tuned RoBERTa transformer model and analyzed their effects on product ratings across ten Amazon product categories. With the rapid advancement of large language models such as GPT-2, AI-generated reviews increasingly resemble authentic customer feedback, threatening consumer trust, marketplace fairness, and product reputations. Drawing on trust theory, Technology Acceptance Model, and behavioral economics, this research designed and evaluated a detection system using a balanced dataset of 40,432 Amazon product reviews equally split between human-written and AI-generated content. The fine-tuned RoBERTa model achieved an extremely high F1-score (f1=0.9714) compared with the Logistic Regression (f1=0.8784) and Support Vector Machine (f1=0.8825) baseline classifiers. Based on the error analysis conducted for this study, false positive predictions were primarily human-written reviews written in an unfavourable manner with an average of 33.11 words, as opposed to the overall mean of 71.77 words for all human-written reviews. Most words were generic in nature and thus matched the language patterns characteristic of AI-generated content. As previously indicated, a one-way ANOVA was performed and found that the proportion of reviews generated by AI had no significant impact on the mean product ratings in 8 out of 10 product categories, with statistically significant effect observed only in Sports & Outdoors and Tools & Home Improvement product categories. Additionally, a proof-of-concept (POC) web application was created to demonstrate the real-time classification of reviews as well as before-and-after comparison of product ratings based on all available content categories. Overall, the study provides a significant amount of evidence to support the use of content-based linguistic detection rather than number of rating-based approaches and thereby provides valuable information for e-commerce sites, policy-makers and researchers about how to address the increasing use of AI-generated content.

title: Fine-Tuning Transformer Models through Data-Augmented Adversarial Learning for AI-Paraphrased Text Detection in Academic Essays
abstract: The continued development of AI-powered paraphrasing tools and the growing use of generative AI for content creation have raised serious concerns about academic integrity. These tools can change the linguistic and structural characteristics of AI-generated text with the goal of avoiding detection by conventional systems, which could result in false negatives and undetected AI abuse. This study proposes a strong AI-powered text detection framework that combines an adversarial learning approach with the contextual analysis capabilities of various transformer model architectures to overcome this difficulty. By exposing both conventional machine learning models and transformer-based models to AI-generated essays that have been paraphrased using various techniques, the proposed framework will undergo the process of adversarial training. These include prompt engineering, back-translation, rule-based paraphrasing, and AI paraphrasing tools (APTs). Adversarial learning is implemented alongside KL-consistency regularization for the transformer models. Traditional models, like SVM and XGBoost were also trained with TF-IDF features as a baseline with data-augmentation techniques. The models are evaluated with standard performance metrics and error analysis corresponding to linguistic changes made by the paraphrasing methods. Furthermore, the attack success rate (ASR) and an accompanying error analysis are used to evaluate the efficacy of various paraphrasing methods. To contribute to more effective AI misuse detection in educational settings, the results intend to demonstrate enhanced detection against AI-generated and AI-paraphrased academic essays

title: GoFare: A Smart Fare Collection and Tracking System for Modernized Jeepneys in Naga City Using a Card-Based Payment System
abstract: GoFare is a card-based fare collection and vehicle tracking system designed for modernized public transportation in Naga City. The system aims to provide a faster, more convenient, and cashless transportation experience for commuters while helping transport operators manage fare collection and vehicle monitoring more efficiently. The system uses RFID technology through reloadable smart cards that allow passengers to pay fares using a tap-and-go process. GoFare also integrates GPS and geofencing technology to track the real-time location of modernized jeepneys and monitor whether vehicles are operating within authorized routes and designated areas. Passengers can register accounts, link their GoFare cards, monitor balances, reload funds through GCash and other e-wallet services, and track vehicle locations. Transport operators and administrators can monitor passenger records, fare collections, and vehicle activity through a centralized dashboard. The study concludes that GoFare can improve fare management, commuter convenience, and transport monitoring by introducing a secure and efficient cashless system for public transportation modernization.

title: Passengers Map — A Smart Mobile Application for Real-Time Public Transportation Tracking
abstract: Public transportation is essential to daily commuting, yet many passengers face challenges with service availability and personal safety, particularly during off-peak and nighttime hours. To address these concerns, this study presents ”Passengers Map,” a mobile application designed to provide real-time GPS-based tracking of public transportation vehicles. By delivering live updates on vehicle locations and estimated arrival times, the application enhances the commuting experience, reduces uncertainty, and strengthens passenger safety - especially for evening and night commutes - while maintaining user convenience and accessibility. This study evaluates the effectiveness of Passengers Map in improving navigation and safety within public transportation systems. While the application demonstrates significant potential, several limitations warrant consideration: dependency on mobile network connectivity that may affect GPS accuracy, initial deployment restricted to a limited user base, and exclusion of private transportation services. Despite these constraints, Passengers Map offers a practical and dependable solution for public transportation users, with the overarching goal of enhancing the overall quality and safety of public transit systems.

title: Beepney: Enhancing Commuter Experience and Safety for Public Transportation through Mobile Platform
abstract: The Philippine system of public transport, most especially within the informal and localized segments of the system, including tricycles, jeepneys, and other public transportation vehicles tends to experience problems concerning the irregularity of fares, poor commuter security, and the lack of operational transparency of the given service. Beepney is a proposed smartphone application that aims to solve these problems in one user-friendly platform that comprises real-time fare calculation, cashless payment, ride-hailing, emergency call systems, and driver verification. In this research, Beepney is designed and developed with a rapidly developing approach (Rapid Application Development, or RAD) in mind, relying on currently popular technologies, including React Native, Supabase, Firebase Cloud Messaging, and the Mapbox API to provide a timely and user-feedback-informed iteration. Modeling and design with Figma and Lucidchart can help with making the interface user-friendly and the system flow understandable, paymongo for integrating cashless payment, whereas GitHub and ClickUp will enable teamwork and project management. In closing the existing commuting gaps in experience, security, and fare predictability, Beepney will provide a safer, more reasonable, and more effective transport journey to both local and visiting travellers in the Philippines.

title: Park-in: Streamlining University Parking Management Operations through Mobile Application
abstract: This study presented the development and assessment of Park-in, a mobile and web application created to solve parking issues experienced by the constituents of the Bagumbayan Campus of the Ateneo de Naga University, Philippines. The application utilizes real-time data to offer users current information on parking availability, ultimately streamlining and enhancing the parking process. The goals of the study were to create a user-friendly application interface, assess its efficacy through systematic data collection and analysis, and gauge its influence on stakeholders such as students, employees, and security personnel. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of Park-in in reducing parking search times, improving the parking experience, and offering distinct advantages over current parking management strategies on the university campus. By focusing on these key areas, the research aims to support a more efficient urban environment, enhance business processes, and reduce traffic congestion. The application has an outstanding result for both the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and System Usability Scale (SUS). The result for UAT is 92.48, which signifies that testers encountered minimal bugs while using the application. Meanwhile, a 74.33 for the SUS result exceeded the industry average System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 68. With these results, most of the users had a great experience while using the app.

title: Incorporating Non-Attractor Constraints in Slime Mould Algorithm for Urban Road Network Optimization
abstract: In order to address growing concerns with traffic congestion in the region, the need for a network of roads has become more pressing than ever within the context of Southeast Asia’s rapid urbanization. Utilizing Naga City as an example for sustainable development in the future, this paper proposes an innovative method to optimize the layout of urban roads using the concept of non-attractors along with the Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA). The methodology employed consists of modeling and prototyping with the help of five stages: (1) collection of data and creation of spatial grid; (2) identifying attractors and non-attractors; (3) forming a biased network connection according to the pattern of foraging behavior of slime mould; (4) refining of the resulting network via implementation of Dijkstra’s algorithm to define the road hierarchy; and (5) adaptation of the network to current infrastructure. According to the sensitivity analysis, the value of the force constant c which maximizes network efficiency without causing unnecessary expenses lies between 10.0 and 22.0. The adapted network led to an increase of total length by only 2.05% (from 443.19 km to 452.28 km) but managed to reduce average travel time by 6.9% and aggregate accessibility costs by 19.3%. In addition, the standard deviation and maximal values of edge betweenness centrality decreased as well, thus spreading the demand uniformly throughout the grid. The proposed algorithm provides a simple and effective solution to the problem at hand with minimal investments from city authorities. In the future, it would be helpful to develop a road hierarchy in accordance with Spectrum Mobility standards as well as integrate local zoning and land use information into the model and validate it through dynamic traffic simulation.

title: Stormwatch: A Real-time Flood Monitoring and Depth Estimation System using an Ensemble of YOLOv11l-seg Model and Surface Normal Estimation Model
abstract: This paper presents the design framework for Stormwatch, a real-time flood estimation system using object segmentation models and surface normal estimatation models. The system comprises several components, such as an edge-based artificial intelligence (AI) module known as Tempest, a centralized flood monitoring platform, and a disaster management system. By leveraging a robust architecture, Stormwatch combines edge computing, cloud services, computer vision, and geographic information systems (GIS) to provide comprehensive flood detection and geometric estimation capabilities. To address harsh challenges such as lack of data, environmental unreliablity and resource constraints, the research methodology employs robust data augmentation, cross-validation, and ensemble learning. Tempest, the important AI component, integrates computer vision models like the YOLOv11 for semantic segmentation to perform classification for flood mapping. This segmentation is combined with monocular surface normal estimation to enable a comprehensive flood assessment.

title: Flood Extent and Depth Prediction in the Bicol River Basin Using Convolutional Long-Short Term Memory (ConvLSTM)
abstract: This study presents a Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) model for predicting flood extent and depth in the Bicol River Basin, a flood-prone region. Existing forecasting efforts in the area primarily focus on rainfall and water level prediction, creating a gap in spatially explicit flood extent and depth mapping that is directly accessible to decision-makers. To address this, the model integrates rainfall forecasts from Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA), outputs from a water level prediction model, and Digital Elevation Model data to capture spatiotemporal flood patterns. Results are presented through a web-based heatmap that visualizes flood depth using a color gradient for easier interpretation. However, prediction accuracy depends on the reliability of forecast inputs. The system operates with an approximate 6-hour lead time, does not cover drainage capacity.

title: Multi-Objective Facility Location Optimization for Efficient Disaster Response using Multi-Modal Transport Network
abstract: Disaster preparedness remains a critical challenge in the Bicol region of the Philippines, where frequent typhoons and floods disrupt accessibility and delay humanitarian response. This study addresses the optimization of relief distribution center locations under uncertainty, accounting for variable demand, supply disruptions, and transportation network vulnerability. By integrating Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data with facility location models, both deterministic and stochastic, the research enhances the spatial accuracy and operational relevance of logistical planning. A detailed network analysis reveals structural fragility in the region’s road infrastructure, particularly in flood-prone areas such as the Bicol River Basin. The proposed stochastic Facility Location Problem (FLP) model, which anticipates spatially correlated disruptions, significantly outperforms its deterministic counterpart - achieving a 77.6% reduction in average travel time and consistently higher Relief Delivery Efficiency (RDE) across multiple disaster scenarios. The findings demonstrate the robustness of certain warehouse locations and underscore the importance of integrating resilience and equity into disaster logistics. Despite improvements in overall efficiency, spatial inequities persist, particularly for remote and vulnerable communities. The study advocates for fairness-aware models and the inclusion of social vulnerability indicators to better balance efficiency with equitable access. Ultimately, a decision-support system with GIS-based visualization is proposed to assist disaster management authorities in making data-informed, just, and resilient decisions on facility placement and emergency response.

title: Alerto+: A Mobile Reporting Application Integrated with Real-Time Web Dashboard for Community Issue and Barangay Response in the Bicol Region
abstract: This paper presents Alerto+, a Barangay-Level Incident and Community Issue Reporting System, aimed at overcoming the obstacles associated with reporting community issues and concerns, enhancing service efficiency, and assuring secure data management. Traditional methods of reporting often discourage citizen participation due to fear, inconvenience, or lack of real-time feedback. To address such limitations, Alerto+ presents a mobile app combined with a secure web-based dashboard for barangay officials and the local government unit (LGU) administration. It includes interactive maps with real-time pin drops, enabling quick visual tracking of issues and a centralized platform for the officials to manage and respond to submissions. Additionally, Alerto+ streamlines document request processing by enabling residents to submit requests and receive status updates, while barangay officials can manage approvals and scheduling within the system. The system also supports broadcasting of barangay announcements, such as typhoon alerts, aid distributions, and power outages, directly to residents, who can follow multiple barangays for timely information. All reports are logged with metadata for traceability, and the system automatically issues warnings or blocks repeat offenders. A review of existing literature reveals gaps in the lack of real-time monitoring and transparency of complaint management. Alerto+ fills these gaps with a modular, scalable, and user-friendly solution built for the realities of communities like those in Naga City. By transforming everyday complaints into actionable data, Alerto+ empowers barangays to act faster, engage more residents, and improve local safety and accountability, redefining how communities participate in governance.

title: SAGE - Solar Assessment and Generation Estimation: A Machine Learning and GIS Approach for Community Energy Planning
abstract: The use of localized solar energy planning is still underdeveloped in various cities in the Philippines, where households are confronted with the increasing cost of electricity and the lack of available pre-assessment procedures. Focusing on Naga City, Camarines Sur (using official administrative boundary shapefile), this study formulated and evaluated SAGE (Solar Assessment and Generation Estimation), which is a framework designed to estimate photovoltaic system capacity (kWp) using open-source geospatial data, PVWatts® physics-based simulations, machine learning (Linear Regression and Random Forest Regression), and integrating it on a web-application within a unified workflow. Machine learning models were trained to approximate standardized photovoltaic energy outputs and applied to generate coordinate-level capacity estimates, to which the results and metrics indicated that the Random Forest model ( R2 = 0.98 ) achieved low error margins closely aligned with the scaled PVWatts-derived outputs compared to the baseline model, Linear Regression (R2 = 0.45 ). Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) was the primary element impacting photovoltaic capacity estimations, according to the random forest model’s feature importance analysis, which is in line with accepted physical principles. The web application (with Random Forest model integration) also produced estimates within a reasonable range for preliminary assessment, in accordance with the conducted limited benchmarking with local solar practitioners while using actual local installer data. Additionally, a usability evaluation within 16 participants of Naga City households suggested that the system is comprehensible and suitable for early-stage planning. Ultimately, the study demonstrated that integrating open-source geospatial data, physics-based simulations, and machine learning into a web application suggests a scalable and transparent solar capacity estimation, offering a practical approach for supporting localized renewable energy planning.

title: Development of Information Systems Plan for Cada Dental Clinic
abstract: Cada Dental Clinic seeks to deliver the highest quality of clinical care and personalized service in a warm and compassionate atmosphere. Dr. Marilyn Cada, the owner, believes that providing excellent service in a timely manner will create relationships that last as long as our smiles. The clinic offers orthodontics, general dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, pediatric dentistry, and prosthodontics. Since the clinic’s inception, they have collected data using the traditional approach of pen and paper. As time passed, the clinic struggled to keep up with the increasing number of patients that came to see them. Therefore, we, the proponents, conducted an interview with the owner of the clinic in order to make a system that will help them in their operations and solve the problems found. The objectives of the proponents for this research is to plan and design a system that would increase the productivity and efficiency of the clinic in performing tasks related to appointment setting, accounting, and patient information management. The proponents aim to design a web prototype that is designed to have systematic and paper free methods for the target client.

title: Enhancing Oral Health Management through Appointment Management and Dental Activity Tracker
abstract: The proposed project introduces an innovative mobile and web-based application to improve oral health management in Camarines Sur by integrating appointment scheduling and an oral health routine tracker. Designed to streamline bookings, track dental practices, and provide a user-friendly platform, the system addresses inefficiencies in manual processes, helping patients maintain consistent oral care and enabling dentists to manage schedules effectively. Testing with 17 respondents yielded above-average usability scores (70.71 for dentists, and 75.75 for patients), demonstrating strong satisfaction and practicality. The application focuses on onboarding, appointment management, oral health tracking, and monitoring, improving efficiency for practitioners and patient experiences. This system represents a significant advancement in organized, patient-centered oral health management, offering a promising solution to challenges in the region.

title: salud.ko: A Mobile-Based Application Bridging the Gaps in Healthcare Access and Information Management for Local Communities
abstract: Despite advancements in technology, local communities such as Naga City, Philippines, still face significant challenges in accessing healthcare services, impacting the overall experiences of the residents. To address these issues, this study entailed the progressive development and completion of salud.ko, a mobile application designed to provide a centralized platform where users can easily locate and connect with healthcare services, including hospitals, clinics, and healthcare providers. It included an emergency hotline functionality for quick access during emergencies and allowed users to manage and track their personal health records. The scope of the application revolved around the healthcare services in Naga City by providing detailed information on local medical professionals, facilities, services, and emergency hotlines. This included the involvement of Bikolanos and health-care providers as participants of the proponents. Agile methodology was used for the development process, incorporating iterative phases of requirements gathering, system analysis, development, testing, deployment, and feedback collection. Tools such as Trello, Flutter, and Github, were utilized in the development of salud.ko. The application was guided by insights gathered from surveys, consultations, and interviews with users and healthcare providers to ensure it met their needs and preferences. Through beta testing, initial user feedback was collected to refine the application, followed by continuous maintenance and updates to adapt to evolving healthcare needs. salud.ko successfully improved the efficiency and accessibility of healthcare services and management in Naga City, addressing local healthcare gaps and contributing to enhanced community well-being.

title: GIYA: Enhancing Accessibility and Support for PWDs through a Responsive Web and Mobile Platform
abstract: Many people with disabilities (PWDs) still encountered obstacles in obtaining basic services such as government or public assistance, employment, education, assistive devices, and healthcare, despite existing legislation intended to protect their rights. The lack of consolidated information and the growing misuse of Persons with Disabilities identification cards contributed to these difficulties. To provide accessibility, support, and empowerment for PWDs, GIYA was developed as a responsive web platform, complemented by a mobile application, designed with a greater purpose. Respondents from different groups received an overview of the application, its purpose, and instructions for accessing it. They completed User Acceptance Testing (UAT), the System Usability Scale (SUS), a short questionnaire, task completion rate assessment, and functionality testing. Participants included 10 PWDs (35.7%), 5 close relatives (17.9%), 5 representatives from establishments (17.9%), and 8 administrators (28.6%). GIYA features digital PWD ID verification via ID number or QR code, tracking of public assistance applications, legal rights education, and real-time program updates, supporting multiple user roles. Results showed strong satisfaction, with an average UAT score of 4.48 (89.87%) and an average SUS score of 77.50 (B+), indicating excellent usability. PWDs completed all tasks successfully, while close relatives and establishment representatives completed most tasks with a few failures. Functionality testing also demonstrated high success rates across all user groups. GIYA improved access to resources, enhanced information accuracy, reduced human processing time, and supported more efficient service delivery. It promoted digital inclusion and empowered PWDs to live with greater independence and dignity.

title: Benchmarking the Impact of Network Parameters on Blockchain Performance: A Simulation Based Study
abstract: Blockchain technology is an ever-growing field in today’s industry because of its decentralized and immutable nature in terms of security. However, it has performance limitations as usage scales. This research investigated the impact of two key network parameters, block size and block generation interval, on blockchain performance using Sim Block, a Java-based blockchain simulator. The study simulated variations in block size (0.5MB, 1MB, 2MB, 3MB, and 4MB), Node count (5, 10, 20, 50), and block generation interval (600 s, 300 s, 120 s, 60 s, and 30 s) to analyze their effects on throughput, latency, and fork rate. Findings were visualized through graphs and charts. By systematically analyzing these parameters, the study provided insights into optimal configurations for blockchain networks. The findings were expected to benefit blockchain developers, researchers, and industries such as finance, healthcare, and supply chain management by offering practical benchmarks to improve scalability and efficiency.

title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Smart Contracts through an Implementation of Decentralized Rental Protocols using NFT Standards on Ethereum Virtual Machine
abstract: The emergence of blockchain technology has not only revolutionized the financial sector but also digital asset ownership through Non-fungible Tokens (NFTs) and smart contracts. Ethereum, as the leader of a digital asset ecosystem with over $89.76 billion in total value locked, has enabled widespread adoption of decentralized applications with diverse utilities in finance, gaming, and governance. ERC-721 and ERC-1155 pioneered the digital asset landscape and are currently the mainstream standards used in decentralized applications on blockchains built with the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM). Despite their widespread adoption, there is a gap in their functionality as rentable assets. Current system implementations for ERC-721 and ERC-1155 rentals are complex, relying on non-standard implementations or without broad ecosystem compatibility. In this case, the Ethereum ecosystem needs a unified protocol for rentals that ensures interoperability across different platforms that utilize the ERC-721 and ERC-1155 standards. This study aims to make blockchain technology understandable through smart contracts, specifically by developing and analyzing a rental mechanism for the aforementioned NFT standards. Moreover, the proposed rental protocol will be implemented on the EVM using Solidity. The approach for the smart contracts will adopt a modular architecture using a factory pattern and two registries, where the factory smart contract manages fees and system deployment, while the registry contracts handle custodial and non-custodial rentals. The smart contracts will be deployed to the Sepolia testnet and assessed for feasibility by a number of users via a website application during a feasibility study, with decentralize application metrics including gas cost, transaction success rate, and task completion rate.

title: A Vendor-Agnostic, Resource-Aware, Explainable Software-Defined Intrusion Prevention System for SOHO Networks using PPO, Policy Distillation, and TreeSHAP-IQ
abstract: Small Office and Home Office (SOHO) networks represent a significant portion of global internet traffic yet remain unprotected due to the resource constraints of typical SOHO gateways, which are not suited for enterprise-grade Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS). This study proposes a vendor-agnostic, resource-aware, and explainable Software-Defined Intrusion Prevention System (SD-IPS) tailored for constrained SOHO environments. The system integrates offline Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based reinforcement learning, policy distillation into a compact tree-based model, and interaction-aware explainability via TreeSHAP-IQ, enforced inline through Open vSwitch (OVS) and Ryu, with targeted deep packet inspection provided by Suricata. The architecture was trained and evaluated using public benchmark datasets (UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017) alongside synthetic SOHO attack scenarios. Four research questions addressed detection effectiveness, performance-overhead trade-offs, explainability consistency, and system scalability under concurrent load. Results indicate that the distilled student model achieves competitive detection performance relative to Suricata and XGBoost baselines while substantially reducing decision latency and resource overhead. Targeted DPI-derived features yielded the largest detection improvements. Explainability analysis revealed moderate-to-high interaction consistency across attack classes (Kendall’s ω ranging from 0.625 to 1.000), supporting its use in analyst triage and operational decision support. Scalability testing confirmed a maximum sustainable throughput of approximately 5.23 flows per second at ten concurrent users, demonstrating that the SD-IPS operates within its intended SOHO deployment envelope.

title: FACT: Detecting Atomics API-Related Concurrency Flaky Tests in JavaScript Applications
abstract: The ubiquity of web services and applications makes JavaScript one of the most prominent programming languages today. In these kinds of web applications, the Atomics API enables multithreading through SharedArrayBuffer objects. Improper management of shared access cause data races, leading to concurrency flaky tests. No contemporary tools exist that can detect flaky tests caused in this way through the Atomics API. This study developed the JavaScript Atomics Source Code Model (JSASCM), an adaptation of the Multithreaded Source Code Model (MASCM), for a static method that detects concurrency flaky tests caused by the Atomics API. Firstly, it identified how flakiness arises from data races caused by non-atomic read-modify-write sequences implemented using Atomics.load and Atomics.store. Secondly, the JSASCM method achieved a significantly higher accuracy than the naive rerun strategy (at 10 reruns) at a much lower cost. The method is still prone to false positives due to inherent limitations discovered in the underlying JSASCM model, but addressing these limitations may be a simple task for future research.

title: TestQuest: An Open Bug Reporting Platform with Developer-Driven Rewards
abstract: Effective software testing remains a problem in areas like Tanzania, despite the ever-evolving software development technologies. The software testers’ scarcity problem, the absence of adequate training opportunities, and little to no encouragement for novice testers have all been associated with poor software reliability and project timelines. This research suggested creating a CST (Crowdsourced Software Testing) platform that allows developers to submit their software for testing while enabling novice testers to find bugs and be compensated. In addition to CST, the platform uses game design features such as points, badges, and leaderboards to increase participation. The project aims to achieve the outlined goals by utilizing Agile Scrum, accepting iterative stakeholder feedback in designated sprint cycles as the basis for continuous enhancement. This methodology incorporates user interface/user experience design, including prototyping, feature implementation, usability testing, and evaluations using survey, observation, and interview techniques. The CST platform is designed to enable various types of testing, including usability, performance, and compatibility testing, as well as mechanisms for bug reporting, test case description, and automation script submission.

title: "TerraTrack": A Mobile Application For Gamifying Eco-Conscious User Engagement
abstract: Climate change is one of the most pressing challenges of our era, propelled by the increasing cluster of greenhouse gases in our atmosphere. While systemic changes are crucial in addressing the climate crisis, collective actions from individuals play an essential role in mitigating its impact. The clear barrier to individual action is the lack of accessible tools, motivation, and strategies to effectively maximize their positive environmental impact. This study addresses the gap by developing “TerraTrack”, a mobile application with gamified systems that focuses on helping users measure their carbon footprint, deepen their knowledge about climate change, and provide personalized routine based on their lifestyle and preferences. The primary objectives of this study are to (1) develop a mobile application with a built-in personal carbon footprint calculator, (2) provide sustainability education through the educational hub with quizzes to support learning, (3) create personalized routine for users to maximize their positive environmental impact, (4) integrate gamified systems as a motivational tool, (5) enable progress tracking through monthly comparisons and community shared goal visualization. The study employed a design and development methodology using the agile development approach. The system’s design was heavily guided by the Octalysis Framework, utilizing most of its core drives, mainly to enhance user motivation, engagement, and retention. These core drives were used throughout the system features such as badges, leaderboards, progress tracking, quizzes, virtual currency, and progress visualization. Usability Testing was conducted using the System Usability Scale (SUS), which involved 21 general users and 3 partner establishments. The results indicate that TerraTrack achieved a high level of usability, receiving SUS scores of 80.71 from user-side testing and 88.33 from partner-side testing. These scores fall under the ”Excellent” and ”Best Imaginable” adjective rating range. In conclusion, TerraTrack showcases the application of the Octalysis Framework, which demonstrates the effectiveness for motivating eco-conscious behavior and sustainability for user engagement. By including gamified elements, the system serves as a tool for promoting environment-responsible habits.

title: Applying Natural Language Processing to Analyze Job Market Skill Demands to Improve Curriculum Alignment
abstract: This study applies Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyze job market skill demands and evaluate their alignment with the Ateneo de Naga University Department of Computer Science (DCS) curriculum. A hybrid skill extraction approach was implemented using TF-IDF, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), RoBERTa-based Named Entity Recognition, and a phrase-based extraction method to capture both single and multi-word technical skills from job postings. The extracted skills were quantified using Demand and Coverage metrics. Demand reflects the frequency of skills in industry job postings, while Coverage represents the extent to which these skills are present in the curriculum. Both metrics were normalized to allow consistent comparison across all skills. A quadrant-based classification framework was then applied to categorize skills into Skill Gap, Aligned, Over-covered, and Low Priority groups. Results show that while core programming and software development skills demonstrate reasonable alignment with the curriculum, several high-demand skills such as cloud technologies, data analytics, and modern frameworks exhibit low coverage, indicating critical gaps. The hybrid model achieved improved recall compared to individual models, providing broader skill coverage, although with slightly reduced precision. The findings highlight the need for continuous curriculum updates to better match evolving industry’s requirements. The proposed system provides a scalable and data-driven approach for academic institutions to monitor curriculum relevance and support evidence-based curriculum enhancement.

title: connext: A Mobile Platform for Centralized Job Search and Recruitment Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Recruitment and selection processes are obstructed by inefficiencies and saturation in online platforms and are hindered by too-long screening and information overload for both employers and job seekers. The study proposes a mobile solution that leverages swipe-based mechanics inspired by dating applications like Tinder to optimize job matching through algorithm-driven decisions. Artificial intelligence and machine learning are utilized specifically – Retrieval-Augmented generation (RAG), whose process is to give comments and improve filters using its ability to understand and provide feedback, and a native messaging system for swift communication between recruiters and job seekers. The platform emphasizes entry into entry-level and stable jobs. While the solution provides an efficient and user-friendly interaction, the project acknowledges that it has limitations, such as reliance on stable internet connectivity, data scarcity in job postings, hallucinations in LLM-generated feedback, competition with already established platforms, and manual verification in the early stage of the application. The study addresses the gap between employer demands for rapid evaluation and job seekers’ need for swift employment, offering an alternative to traditional and saturated recruitment platforms.

title: Partner Portal: Managing Company Partnerships for Student Internships through Web Application
abstract: Internship programs play a vital role in connecting academic knowledge into real-world experience. However, as technology continues to advance rapidly, the conventional process of accrediting partnered companies such as Host Training Establishments (HTEs) often results in delayed approvals, miscommunication, and operational inefficiencies for universities, companies, and students. As a result, the process resulted in slow processing time, and limited access to verified partner companies led to missed opportunities and confusion during coordination. To address these challenges, this study aimed to develop the Partner Portal, a web-based application designed to streamline the internship and partnership process. The system provided companies with a platform to apply as Host Training Establishments (HTEs), track their application status, and evaluate student interns. At the same time, students gain access to a verified list of Host Training Establishments (HTEs), allowing them to view the requirements of each organization, apply for internships, and submit requirements in a structured manner. Furthermore, the system enhances communication among stakeholders, ensures smooth data management, and fostered collaboration between academia and industry. Overall, this project aimed to increase efficiency, transparency, and reliability in internship program management, serving as a practical solution for organizations that planned to modernize their internship processes.

title: EduCart: A Marketplace Platform for Universities
abstract: University communities often face challenges in acquiring affordable academic resources due to reliance on scattered social media groups and informal networks that lack trust and organization. This study introduces EduCart, a web-and-mobile marketplace platform designed exclusively for universities, enabling students, faculty, alumni, organizations, and businesses to buy, sell, rent, trade, pasabuy, and request emergency lending within a secure university-verified ecosystem. The platform integrates role-based authentication via university email, real-time messaging, peer reviews, courier tracking, and an escrow system that rewards safe transactions. Specialized features include emergency lending for urgent academic needs, rental scheduling, giveaway systems, and dedicated sections for student businesses and organizations. A tiered commission model and subscription options support long-term sustainability.

title: Foodies: A Mobile Application for Efficient Food Ordering in School Environments
abstract: This study presents Foodies, a mobile application designed to improve the food ordering and delivery experience in school environments. Traditional canteen systems often involve long queues, limited vendor reach, and inefficient service during peak hours. Foodies addresses these issues by offering a digital platform where students, faculty, and staff can browse menus, place orders for pickup or delivery, and track order status in real time. The application also introduces a student-run delivery system, allowing enrolled students to earn income as delivery runners while following performance and safety standards. Vendors are required to undergo approval and maintain food quality and menu accuracy. The system includes features such as user verification, secure payment processing, and real-time notifications. Developed using React Native and Supabase, the app supports Android devices and offers scalable database and authentication services. By digitizing food services on campus, Foodies aims to reduce wait times, support student employment, and provide a more convenient and efficient food ordering process. This project also contributes to the ongoing shift toward campus-level digital ecosystems in response to changing consumer behavior and post-pandemic service expectations.

title: Culina: An AI-Powered Food Application based on User Inventory
abstract: Culina is an AI-powered mobile application that generates personalized recipe suggestions based on ingredients available at home. The system utilizes Natural Language Processing (NLP) to analyze user-provided ingredient lists entered manually, and then matches these with a large recipe database and ML models to propose complete meals. Leveraging techniques such as multi-input neural networks and transformer-based language models, the app adapts recommendations to user dietary preferences and nutritional goals. By training on comprehensive recipe datasets and refining outputs through user feedback, Culina aims to reduce food waste and improve cooking convenience.

title: Bahayahay: A Web Application towards a Comprehensive Property Listing and Review Mechanism in the Philippine Real Estate Market
abstract: Bahayahay is a property listing platform that addresses common problems such as unlicensed real estate agents illegally selling properties and public property listings with missing documents. To ensure that only legitimate brokers and salespersons are on the platform, Bahayahay requires all realtors to submit their Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and (DHSUD) IDs and/or accreditation. For independent listings, such as pre-owned homes or build-and-sell projects, the platform has a strict document screening process. This prevents properties with issues, such as unpaid estate taxes or incomplete transfers of ownership, from being made available for sale. Beyond verification, Bahayahay also introduces features that are still missing in many local property websites. These include built-in messaging and review systems, inspired by the Proptech 2.0 movement. These features make communication easier and give buyers more confidence in their choices. Bahayahay combines rigorous checks with user-centric features for residents of Naga City, Camarines Sur.

title: Dormease: A Centralized Web and Mobile System for Dormitory Search, Management, and Accreditation
abstract: Finding suitable housing is a persistent challenge, with many dormers relying on outdated and inefficient methods such as word-of-mouth referrals and onsite visitations. Dormitory owners also face difficulties in promoting their properties, while accrediting institutions continue to rely on manual accreditations. These inefficiencies result in dormers settling for what is available, dorm owners struggling with low visibility, and accreditation processes that are time-consuming and labor-intensive. This study proposes the development of Dormease, a web and mobile platform that provides a centralized and technology-driven solution for dorm searching, property listing and management, and accreditation. The system will feature comprehensive dormitory listings, map integration, real-time messaging, visit scheduling, dormitory management, and an accreditation system, ensuring a streamlined searching process for dormers while improving efficiency for dorm owners and institutions. This study will involve designing, developing, and implementing a platform that will initially cater to dormitories within Naga City, with accreditation features limited to dormitory owners seeking verification through Ateneo de Naga University. While the system primarily targets students looking for accommodation, it is also accessible to faculty members, professionals, and other individuals in need of long-term housing. By bridging the gap between dormers, dormitory owners, and accrediting institutions, Dormease aims to improve the overall housing experience through a digitalized and user-friendly approach.

title: AMPAT: Arduino-based Wired Home Security System for Small Area Houses
abstract: Home Security has become a common problem among homeowners in other countries and the Philippines. Burglars or thieves can be seen everywhere, hiding in plain sight, planning and targeting vulnerable houses, and proceeding to do malicious acts to satisfy their needs. They intend to exploit the opportunity to steal items and assets that can be sold or exchanged. Some homeowners provide some security measures to prevent this malicious activity by installing CCTV or Smart security gadgets. The proposed system aimed to help homeowners provide a feasible option to the home security management system market by introducing a low-cost budget home security system. It provided accurate readings of environment data and on-the-spot detection and alarm activation that made it on par with the capabilities of some home security systems. It also provided real-time notification to its user if the system was triggered and a function to call agencies or offices to provide support to the user. All data that was gathered by the system can be accessed in a web application that only the user and system administrator have access to.

title: A Web-Based Indoor Environment Monitoring System
abstract: Historical wooden artifacts and paper-based documents are highly susceptible to irreversible deterioration due to fluctuations in temperature and humidity. These materials, preserved in galleries, museums, and archives, are essential to a nation’s cultural identity. In cities like Naga, where typhoons and flooding are common, the risks of environmental instability are heightened making real-time monitoring crucial for preservation. Traditional monitoring systems are often manual, labor-intensive, and lack real-time responsiveness, limiting their effectiveness in managing indoor conditions. This study proposes a web-based indoor environment monitoring system designed to support preventive maintenance in heritage sites and other climate-sensitive indoor spaces. The system utilizes low-power DHT22 sensors and ESP32 microcontrollers to collect real-time temperature and humidity data. This data is transmitted via Wi-Fi to a cloud-based database using Firebase and visualized through a user-friendly web interface. Key system features include live device monitoring, customizable alert thresholds, rule management, and downloadable environmental reports. The Preserv system is designed to be scalable and applicable to other environments that require strict indoor climate regulation, such as laboratories, healthcare storage, and archival facilities. This solution aims to reduce manual workload, provide data-driven recommendations, and support long-term preservation through real-time environmental awareness.

title: PigKeep: A QR-Enabled Pig Farm Monitoring and Management System
abstract: Effective information management is crucial in the pig farming industry for maintaining accurate records and efficient operations. Transitioning from manual paper-based record-keeping to a digital system using a mobile and web application can reduce errors and streamline data entry. With the growing usage of technology, utilizing both mobile and web applications for recording pig data such as pig information, feed inventory, medicine, and financial records can be advantageous for pig farmers. By utilizing a mobile and web application, pig farmers can increase productivity by having access to information anywhere on the farm and at home, respectively. This project had involved the implementation of pig farm information management system through a mobile application, enabled with QR code technology, that allowed pig farm owners and caretakers to seamlessly manage their operations by adding, scanning QR codes, updating, and deleting pig information, feed inventory, medicine inventory, and financial records. In addition to this, a web application is utilized for pig farm owners alone to have a better overview, analysis, and visualization of pig farm records by providing charts and data tables. The web application has the capability to add, update, and delete records in the system. PigKeep works by pig farm owners or caretakers adding their pigs in the system. Each pig is given a unique number and QR code for identification purposes. Users are required to download and print the QR code on a waterproof sticker, which should be attached to a pig ear tag. This ear tag, with the printed waterproof QR code stickers is then attached to the pig’s ear. This allowed users to easily scan the QR code to access and manage the pig’s and pig farm’s information while on-site. With this, pig farm owners and caretakers eliminate the recording inefficiencies and boost their productivity in managing their pig farms.

title: Anomaly Detection in Telemetry Data Logging for Personalized Driving Behavior Feedback in Simulation Racing Video Game
abstract: This paper attempts to implement anomaly detection techniques to provide feedback based on the telemetry data of a simulation racing game. Although telemetry is widely available in most racing video games, interpreting and analyzing it corresponds to a steep learning curve, making it difficult for beginners and novice players to leverage the data to enhance their skills. This study demonstrates the features of two anomaly detection techniques, the Isolation Forest Algorithm and the Local Outlier Factor, by detecting whether they are anomalous or not compared to a large dataset. A lap will be classified as an anomaly when the lap time deviates from the pattern observed in the given data set. The anomalous features were observed, determining how they may contribute to lap performance. In return, with the help of a fuzzy system, the model generates a feedback response on improving driving performance by addressing the detected anomalies, whether a positive or negative attribute or habit that might need to be changed or maintained. This whole process was implemented through a system named CruiserPedia. User testing shows that the users had a favorable response to the study, specifically its process and system, which helped them improve performance in terms of their response to the survey and their driving times. The psycho-metric survey showed a strong positive reception, with all questions receiving a mean score of 5. In contrast, in terms of the open-ended questions, it showed that the CruiserPedia program was helpful as a personal feedback provider and also a software tool for beginner to novice drivers. However, integrating or implementing some of the suggestions of the participants could significantly enhance the program’s effectiveness and usability in its future iteration if it becomes a product in the future.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Data Augmentation Techniques on MobileNetV3-Based Infant Cry Classification in Controlled Indoor Environments
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of multiple data augmentation techniques based on the performance of the MobileNetV3 model for infant cry classification. We explored noise injection, pitch shifting, and time stretching individually and in pairwise combinations to determine which of the augmentation strategies optimizes classification accuracy, latency, and robustness in controlled indoor environments. Models were trained on mel-spectrogram representations of infant cries, incorporating class weighting to address data set imbalance, and also applied different hyperparameter strategies to improve its performance evaluated by using stratified splits and metrics including macro-f1 score, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score. The best model from the experimental phases was integrated to a mobile application and was tested on various controlled indoor settings. Findings revealed that MobileNetV3 performs better for infant cry binary detection than in need-based multiclass classification. For the augmentation techniques, MobileNetV3 model trained on noise-augmented dataset performed the best with 0.5810 macro-f1 score, while among the pairwise augmentation techniques, noise addition + pitch shift yielded the best macro-f1 score of 0.6076. Though this study established that augmentation techniques can improve model performance, it was also shown that some augmentation techniques outperform others and aggressive augmentation may worsen model performance.

title: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Tool-Calling Agents in MCP Environments
abstract: Since its nascent phase, one of LLMs’ major issues has been their inability to interact with the external world or perform dynamic tasks beyond their static training data. This was later addressed through tool-calling setups, allowing the models to invoke functions (tools) to perform tasks it cannot originally do on their own. More recent advancements have introduced major leap with the emergence of Model Context Protocol (MCP), which standardizes LLM-Tool interaction through a universal function-calling mechanism. This enables LLMs to perform actions defined by the developers: tools that are interoperable and easily manageable. As a result, models specializing in tool-calling have become more relevant for many agentic tasks. While mainstream, larger models are performing pretty well, smaller, developer-friendly models are still facing challenges. These include: (1) struggles with maintaining consistency, especially for multi-step workflows; (2) a lack of tool usage decision-making capability; (3) embedding limitations to smart environments. Existing solutions encompass data synthesis and distillation-based approaches, including MCP server utilization for no-training distillation and model rerouting. By building on top of these current solutions, we propose ShrinkMCP - a response-level knowledge distillation framework using Supervised Fine-tuning(SFT) for tool-calling models in MCP-powered systems. In this work, we outline the design of ShrinkMCP and detail its application in distilling tool-use capabilities for both multimodal and text-only models. To demonstrate its viability, our framework can be applied to MCP servers, showing how student models can learn consistent, efficient tool usage from stronger teachers.

title: MARQ: A Multi-Agent Rainbow Deep Q-Networks Framework using AAREN for Mastering Imperfect Information Games
abstract: This research presents MARQ, a Multi-Agent Rainbow Deep Q-Networks, designed to master imperfect information games through the board game Stratego. MARQ leverages a Deep Recurrent Q-Network (DRQN) architecture and league-based self-play training to address the large state space of Stratego and hidden information challenges. The architecture integrates an Attention as Recurrent Neural Network (AAREN) module that produces learned embeddings from observed opponent behavior, enabling implicit piece identity inference through end-to-end training. The system employs Distributional Reinforcement Learning with Noisy Networks to balance strategic unpredictability and stability. The methodology involves developing a game environment and training the AI agent through multi-channel state representations, incorporating AAREN-generated embeddings for hidden information modeling and weighted piece values computed through systematic power analysis to optimize decision making under uncertainty. A structured participant study introduces enthusiasts without prior Stratego experience to create a synchronized learning environment, combining quantitative metrics including win rate percentage, average game length, and decision-making speed, with qualitative usability assessments across performance, reliability, and applicability dimensions. Through this study MARQ aims to deliver strategic decisions comparable to human opponents.

title: "NAGA-ARAM" : An Online Application, Renewal, and Decision Support System on Scholarship Grant Classification of Naga’s Tertiary Scholarship Program
abstract: In Naga City, the Scholarship Division under the Education, Scholarships and Sports Office (ESSO), which facilitates the processes of the Naga Tertiary Scholarship Program (NTSP), has not yet made a transition to online processing of its scholarship application and renewal system. With this, NAGA-ARAM was developed to bring the scholarship application, renewal, and booking processes on a web-based platform that the scholars and applicants can access anytime and anywhere. The profile management provided by the project aimed to improve record keeping and security. NAGA-ARAM also aimed to serve as a Decision Support System (DSS) for an efficient classification and qualification of the scholarship grants for the application process, performance assessment of scholars, and identification of the grant status based on the scholars’ General Weighted Average (GWA) to eliminate repetitive and time-consuming tasks. A dashboard was developed to address the problem on platform for official announcements. Upon the completion of the user testing, results and feedback were gathered. The study revealed that 85% of the respondents were able to accomplish all the tasks successfully and that the system was efficient and effective with an 86.6 overall System Usability Scale (SUS) average. It was recommended that the user interface must be improved, the system must provide supplementary user input fields and options, add content and information, and that the generation of a Certificate of Scholarship be included.

title: HashFlow: Digitized Workflow System
abstract: This project proposed developing a web-based Workflow system to streamline the form approval process. It seeks to make the manual approval process of forms collaborative, more efficient, and convenient. It attempts to provide a platform where users can create an approval workflow and send it for approval to the concerned individuals or offices. The project envisions setting logic to the approval workflows to ensure that approvers receive only relevant requests. It sets parallel or sequential approval flow to ensure administrators only approve once others endorse them. Notifications are sent by email and approved with a single click. Workflows created can be saved for future use.

title: Developing A Mobile Proximity Pet Adoption App
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the digitalization of various sectors, including online shopping and food deliveries. However, the realm of mobile platforms for pet adoption has not fully embraced this transformation, leading to issues and conflicts when relying solely on social media for pet adoption transactions. To tackle this challenge, researchers developed a location-based mobile application using Dart, Flutter, and Firebase, integrating Google Maps Platform for proximity services. The goal was to digitize and streamline the pet adoption process. A group of 31 participants tested the application and provided feedback, emphasizing the need for feature and functionality improvements. Notably, the inclusion of a notification system was recommended. Nonetheless, the overall user experience was deemed user-friendly and intuitive. Users were introduced to the application’s objectives, provided with APK files, and given access to download the app from the Google PlayStore. Registration and login processes were smooth, although some users required additional guidance on certain features. It is worth noting that the application had identified weaknesses, such as occasional maintenance issues with the Firebase Database and Storage, as well as difficulties in sending verification codes due to poor internet connectivity. Moreover, certain development packages used in the application may become deprecated, necessitating regular maintenance. Despite these challenges, the application remains a valuable tool for future pet adoption processes. With high ratings in both the System Usability Scale (SUS) and User Acceptance Testing (UAT), it proves to be a reliable platform for both individuals and organizations engaged in pet-related activities. Overall, this application addresses the limitations of relying solely on social media platforms and offers a convenient and efficient solution for facilitating pet adoptions.

title: KILOS: A Digital Solution for Effective Youth Officials Management in Local Government Units
abstract: Inefficient workflow, lack of transparency, and limited community engagement pose a significant challenge to local youth officials. This project presents KILOS, a web-based information system designed to streamline processes and support community members and local government officials through a centralized platform. KILOS provides features such as project and ordinance publication, budget tracking, public feedback mechanisms, and administrative management tools to improve accessibility and accountability. KILOS was developed following standard software development practices and was deployed as a web application for real-world use. The usability of the system was scored through the System Usability Scale (SUS) and thematic analysis. The system received an SUS score of 78.07 indicating good to excellent usability. Qualitative feedback helped the system identify points of improvement for optimization of system performance and interface enhancements. In general, the results show that KILOS is an effective and user-friendly platform that improves transparency, participation, and efficiency in youth governance provided by local youth officials.
